commitResults.messageTitle: Add person needed to be modified to add students
commitResults.messageBody:
Since TutorEasy has tutors as its target audience, the person class was
modified to include the attributes of a student. The attributes added
are subjects, cost and lesson. The subjects attribute is a set of
subjects that the student is taking, the cost attribute is the cost of
the lesson and the lesson attribute is the day and time of the lesson.
The add command was also modified to include these attributes when
adding a new student. The edit command was also modified to include
 these attributes when editing a student. The person card was also
 modified to display these attributes when viewing a student.

are correctly represented in the string output.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add MVP use cases to Developer Guide
commitResults.messageBody:
Add full use case specifications for the core MVP features in the Developer Guide.
Every use case includes a main success scenario (MSS) together with relevant
alternative and failure extensions.

System, actor and common preconditions are declared globally before the use‑case
section to eliminate redundant documentation.

The following use cases are added:
- Add a student
- Delete a student
- Tag a student
- View timetable
- Find students

* find c/<keyword> to search students by lesson.

commitResults.messageTitle: Tag commands: Add tag management workflow
commitResults.messageBody:
Students can store tags, but they cannot manage them incrementally.

Add tag and untag commands with index validation and duplicate checks.

Enforce tag format and count limits across parsing and storage.

Preserve insertion order so tag data and displays stay predictable.

Accept only -all for removing every tag and reject --all as invalid.

commitResults.messageTitle: Tag commands: Add automated test coverage
commitResults.messageBody:
Tag operations introduce new validation and command failure paths.

Cover command execution, parsing, persistence, and model constraints.

Verify invalid formats, duplicate tags, absent tags, and count limits.

commitResults.messageTitle: Student cards: Style tags as filled labels
commitResults.messageBody:
Plain tag text does not clearly separate labels from student details.

Render tags as compact green labels with spacing that matches the mockup.

The user guide does not describe incremental tag management.

Document tag and untag syntax, validation limits, and space handling.

commitResults.messageTitle: Tag tests: Cover remaining non-UI paths
commitResults.messageBody:
Several non-UI tag paths remain uncovered in Codecov.

Cover command formatting and the remaining equality branch.

Verify invalid untag indexes and direct enforcement of the tag limit.

commitResults.messageTitle: Student cards: Apply tag styles declaratively
commitResults.messageBody:
PersonCard assigns tag styles in Java.

This presentation-only path remains uncovered in headless CI.

Move the styling hook into FXML and target it from CSS.

Keep the established rendering path while preserving filled tag labels.

Preserve tag and untag workflows while integrating student details and extended find support.

Keep tag order, validation, storage checks, and styling. Preserve subject, cost, and lesson data across tag updates, and migrate legacy camel-case tags during loading.
